issue.title: wait_checks resolves 883 dead-runner waiting.json markers every run (~29s), convoying the waits routine

task_type_fields.impact:
About 97% of each `wait_checks` run is wasted on agents that will never resume. The
resulting ~29 s runs convoy the whole `waits` routine (24.4 s cycles), which delays
dependency release and sidecar syncing for live waiters and burns host I/O on a machine
already at load ~20. This is a prerequisite for running `wait_checks` on a fast,
event-driven cadence.
task_type_fields.repro:
`wait_checks` walks every `ace-run` artifact directory in every project and resolves every
`waiting.json` without a `ready.json`, with no runner-liveness filter
(`src/sase/scripts/_chop_wait_checks_run.py:88-135`). Killed or abandoned runners leave
their `waiting.json` behind forever.

Reproduce on athena (2026-10-07):

- The `wait_checks` run at 13:34:52 took 29.2 s:
  `projects=37 artifacts=16858 waiting=907 already_ready=92 invalid=134 unresolved=680 ready_written=1`.
- A liveness check of every `waiting.json` against its `agent_meta.json` `pid`
  (`os.kill(pid, 0)`) gave 906 markers: 19 live runners, 883 dead, 4 with no PID, and
  884 older than 7 days.

Combined with the `waits` tick barrier (`lumberjack.py:227-235`), this ~29 s run (plus
`bead_claim_checks` at ~33 s and `sidecar_auto_sync` at ~15–25 s) stretches the 10 s
`waits` lane to a 24.4 s average cycle. There is "Tick overrun" nearly every cycle.

Suggested fix:

- Enumerate waiters from the artifact index (`write_waiting_marker` already updates it)
  instead of walking all history.
- Skip markers whose runner is dead, using PID plus start identity to avoid PID reuse.
- Add a housekeeping sweep that archives `waiting.json` for runners dead longer than N
  hours.

Verify first that revived or refreshed runners re-resolve before parking and record their
PID before they could be filtered. Check whether `bead_claim_checks`'s 33 s runtime has
the same full-history cause.
